overall_assessment: The candidate follows the approved canonical cutover: one Channel send operation, one common outbound path, one Message owner, and a bounded Meta-private protocol implementation rather than a consumer-level bridge. It is suitable to proceed through the explicitly pending delivery gates, not to claim delivery completion.
recommended_path: Retain the candidate and complete the approved module consolidation, canonical diff-guard authorization/run, preserved-local migration/runtime validation, assisted operator proofs, and remaining final assurance gates before delivery.

findings.title: Required canonical diff guard and module consolidation remain open
findings.rationale: The package explicitly leaves the full canonical diff guard unrun because it requires a separately approved private-boundary exception, and module consolidation is only proposed. These are required cutover conditions, so current source/test evidence cannot establish final canonical delivery state.
findings.suggested_action: Obtain the bounded inspection authority, run and record the canonical diff guard, then apply and verify the approved module consolidation before seeking delivery clearance.

findings.title: Preserved-local runtime and assisted operator proof remain unperformed
findings.rationale: E64 proves a disposable PostgreSQL/BFF/browser candidate with an owned fake provider, but DOD-11 and DOD-12 still require the separately authorized preserved-local migration/runtime binding and operator-performed first-send/reply evidence. The package correctly does not substitute synthetic evidence for those gates.
findings.suggested_action: After the required assurance and runtime-plan approvals, execute the bounded preserved-local migration/provenance and assisted own-channel proof plan; retain delivery as blocked if an eligible approved asset is unavailable.
